text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". Most people with high blood pressure do not feel any warning signs.
When blood pressure reaches extremely high levels (generally above 180/120 mm Hg), the body may show symptoms. This is a medical emergency.

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Severe headache (sudden and intense, or persistent early-morning headaches)
Vision changes (blurry vision, double vision, or eye pain)
Heart palpitations or a pounding sensation in the chest, neck, or ears
Signs of a stroke (such as sudden facial drooping, slurred speech, or weakness in an arm or leg)

text_blocks.snippet: You cannot reliably tell if your blood pressure is high without measuring it with a cuff. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, blood pressure categories are defined as follows:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Stage 2 Hypertension: 140/90 mm Hg or higher
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180/120 mm Hg (Seek emergency care immediately if accompanied by symptoms)

text_blocks.snippet: Learn more about tracking your numbers and guidelines from the American Heart Association or consult the Mayo Clinic.

If you are experiencing symptoms or have a high reading, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately if your blood pressure is over 180/120 mm Hg with chest pain, shortness of breath, or weakness.
